Live: Abhijeet Dipke calls for Tiranga march at Delhi's CP on October 16Anti-ECI Protest Live: Welcome to our live coverage of the latest developments in the escalating standoff between the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and the authorities over demands for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The controversy has intensified after CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody following their protest at Jantar Mantar, where they entered a denotified protest site and waved the Tricolour. While Delhi Police has cited repeated violations of peace bonds and concerns over public order, the CJP and opposition leaders have accused the government of using its machinery to suppress dissent. Congress MP Rahul Gandhi has condemned the arrests, alleging that protesters were assaulted during police action and urging students to preserve video evidence. He also met injured protesters, including a Delhi University student who alleged that she suffered hearing damage after being assaulted during detention. Meanwhile, former chief ministers Mamata Banerjee and MK Stalin have expressed solidarity with the detained CJP leaders, with the latter offering legal assistance. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has thanked Rahul Gandhi for raising the issue, while the party maintains that its campaign for electoral transparency will continue. In a fresh show of support, student organisations SFI and DYFI marched towards Jantar Mantar on Wednesday, demanding Kumar's resignation and calling to reclaim the protest site. The Indian Youth Congress has also stepped up its campaign, putting up hoardings carrying the slogan "Shiv ki Baraat" in central Delhi. Separately, petitions filed by Rahul Gandhi and nine other Opposition leaders challenging the functioning of the Election Commission may be heard by the Supreme Court on October 26, though the date remains subject to formal listing. As political reactions intensify and questions over the arrests and restrictions mount, the focus remains on the CJP's next move and the wider Opposition campaign against the Election Commission. The India Today Desk brings you the latest updates, statements and ground reports as the row unfolds.
